BUYER GUIDE / BY KUMAR SAURABH MISHRA

Find the friction before changing the look.

A redesign brief is stronger when it identifies the decisions visitors struggle to make.

By Kumar Saurabh Mishra, founder of SiteSutra. Planning examples are original demonstrations.

Review the customer journey

Can a first-time visitor explain the offer, see relevant proof, and find the next step? Check mobile reading, broken links, slow pages, and enquiry friction.

Keep useful foundations

Inventory existing content, URLs, search visibility and integrations. Plan redirects where URLs change and preserve content that still serves buyers.

Define a meaningful outcome

Pick specific improvements: clearer services, stronger case studies, easier content editing, or a working enquiry route. Use verified observations to evaluate the result, without assuming design alone will create growth.

Inventory before replacing

Hypothetical home-repair website: /index.html is the homepage, /services.html combines two services, /contact-us.html receives enquiries and /offer-2023.html is obsolete. Inventory content, inbound links, indexability and the visitor task before choosing to keep, merge, redirect or retire each URL.

Hypothetical redirect plan — not configured on SiteSutra
Old URLProposed destinationDecision
/index.html/301 to equivalent home
/services.html/services/301 to retained overview
/contact-us.html/contact/301 to enquiry route
/offer-2023.htmlNoneReview links, then retire with 410 if no replacement exists

Do not send every old URL to the homepage. Test status codes, final destinations and redirect chains; update internal links and sitemap URLs.

Download sample URL inventory · Download sample redirect map

Accept the migration deliberately

Test important old URLs, preserved content, enquiry delivery, canonical host, crawler access, keyboard navigation and narrow screens. Compare real observations before and after release without assuming a redesign creates growth. Discuss a website redesign.
